name: PHYRE
desc: Classic 2D physics puzzles where the agent places one object and the simulator resolves the outcome, scored by AUCCESS over attempt budgets.

name: CLEVRER
desc: Descriptive, explanatory, predictive and counterfactual questions over synthetic collision videos, separating perception from causal reasoning.

name: IntPhys
desc: Violation-of-expectation videos testing object permanence, shape constancy and continuity by comparing plausibility scores of matched possible and impossible clips.

name: IntPhys 2
desc: Photorealistic successor to IntPhys covering permanence, immutability, spatio-temporal continuity and solidity, where current video models stay near chance.

name: Physion
desc: Asks whether an agent can predict object contact in rigid, soft, cloth and fluid scenarios, benchmarked directly against human observers.

name: Physion++
desc: Extends Physion to predictions that require inferring latent mechanical properties such as mass, friction, elasticity and deformability from observed motion.

name: ContPhy
desc: Continuum-physics reasoning over fluids, ropes and deformable objects, a regime where rigid-body-trained models degrade sharply.

name: NEWTON
desc: Tests whether language models hold physical attribute knowledge about everyday objects at the granularity a manipulation planner would need.

name: PhysBench
desc: Four-domain, nineteen-task audit of vision-language models on physical world understanding, with a large measured gap to human accuracy.

name: PhysGame
desc: Uses glitch videos from games to test whether video LLMs can localize and explain violations of physical commonsense rather than describe surface content.

name: Physics-IQ
verifier: Pixel-space metrics vs. real held-out future
desc: Scores generative video models against real filmed continuations of the same scene using spatial and spatio-temporal IoU and MSE, decoupling realism from physics.

name: ERQA
caps: spatial; trajectory; action; state estimation; pointing; multi-view
desc: Embodied Reasoning QA: 400 multiple-choice questions over the reasoning primitives a robot policy consumes, released with the Gemini Robotics report.

name: Cosmos-Reason1
scale: Physical common sense + embodied reasoning suites
caps: physical common sense; embodied reasoning; ontology
desc: Ships an explicit physical-common-sense ontology (space, time, fundamental physics) and paired embodied-reasoning benchmarks across human, robot and driving egocentric video.

name: EgoPlan-Bench
desc: Next-action selection from real egocentric videos with long visual histories, isolating planning from low-level control.

name: EgoPlan-Bench2
desc: Broadens egocentric planning evaluation to daily-life scenarios and shows multimodal LLMs remain far below human performance without task-specific tuning.

name: VideoPhy
desc: Scores generated videos for semantic adherence and physical commonsense across solid-solid, solid-fluid and fluid-fluid interactions.

name: VideoPhy-2
desc: Action-centric successor with per-video physical-rule annotation and a hard split on which all evaluated generators score poorly.

name: PhyGenBench
desc: Organizes text-to-video evaluation by explicit physical law (mechanics, optics, thermal, material) with a three-stage automatic judging pipeline.

name: WorldModelBench
verifier: Fine-tuned VLM judge aligned to human
caps: instruction following; physics adherence; world modeling
desc: Judges video generators as world models on instruction following and physical-law adherence across robotics, driving, industrial and human-activity domains.

name: PhyWorldBench
desc: Covers basic, composite and deliberately anti-physics scenarios so a model cannot score well by defaulting to familiar dynamics.

name: WorldScore
desc: Unifies 3D, 4D and video world-generation models under one protocol measuring controllability, quality and dynamics over generated camera trajectories.

name: EVA
desc: Evaluates whether models can anticipate embodied futures in video across human and robot domains rather than only describe the present frame.

name: VSI-Bench (Thinking in Space)
caps: visual-spatial intelligence; cognitive maps; metric estimation
desc: Tests metric and relational spatial reasoning from egocentric walkthrough video, including distance, size, order and route questions.

name: BLINK
desc: Fourteen classic perception tasks (relative depth, correspondence, multi-view, forensics) reformatted as questions that humans solve at a glance.

name: SpatialRGPT-Bench
desc: Region-grounded spatial QA with ground-truth 3D annotations spanning indoor, outdoor and simulated scenes, scoring both relations and metric distances.

name: EmbSpatial-Bench
desc: Egocentric spatial-relation QA built from embodied simulator scenes, targeting the relations a navigation or manipulation policy must resolve.

name: RoboSpatial
desc: Spatial reasoning annotated in ego-, object- and world-centric frames, and shows the frame choice changes which model wins.

name: Where2Place (RoboPoint)
desc: Free-space referring task where a model must emit image points satisfying a relational instruction, scored against human-annotated masks.

name: RefSpatial-Bench (RoboRefer)
desc: Grades spatial referring by the number of reasoning steps an instruction requires, exposing failure as anchor chains get longer.

name: MMSI-Bench
desc: Multi-image spatial intelligence questions requiring integration across viewpoints, with an annotated error taxonomy for diagnosing failures.

name: OmniSpatial
caps: dynamic reasoning; perspective taking; spatial interaction
desc: Cognition-grounded spatial benchmark spanning dynamic reasoning, complex spatial logic, spatial interaction and perspective taking.

name: SQA3D
desc: Situated QA in real 3D scans: the agent must first localize itself from a described situation, then answer from that pose.

name: ScanQA
desc: 3D question answering over ScanNet point clouds requiring object grounding rather than 2D image cues.

name: EmbodiedQA
desc: The original active-QA formulation: an agent must navigate a simulated house to gather the evidence needed to answer a question.

name: OpenEQA
caps: episodic memory QA; active QA; real scans
desc: Open-vocabulary EQA over real scanned homes in two modes, episodic-memory and active exploration, scored by an LLM judge calibrated to humans.

name: HM-EQA (Explore until Confident)
desc: Multiple-choice EQA in Habitat-Matterport scenes that scores when an agent decides it has seen enough, not only whether the answer is right.

name: EXPRESS-Bench
desc: Penalizes agents that answer correctly without having actually observed the evidence, by jointly scoring exploration trajectory and answer.

name: RoboVQA
caps: robot video QA; affordance; success detection
desc: Long-horizon robot and human video QA covering planning, affordance, success detection and remaining-step estimation from a real deployment setting.

name: ALFRED
desc: Maps free-form English directives to sequences of navigation and interaction actions in AI2-THOR, with an unseen-scene split that still separates methods.

name: ALFWorld
desc: Aligns a TextWorld abstraction with ALFRED scenes so policies can be trained in text and evaluated on embodied execution; the default cheap harness for LLM agents.

name: VirtualHome
desc: Represents household activities as executable programs in a simulated home, the substrate for much later LLM task-planning evaluation.

name: BEHAVIOR-1K
caps: long-horizon household; mobile bimanual manipulation; physics fidelity
desc: Thousand human-surveyed household activities in a full-physics Omniverse simulator, with goals expressed as logical predicates over object states.

name: BEHAVIOR Challenge
desc: Standing competition on full-length BEHAVIOR household tasks with released human teleoperation demonstrations and a partial-credit metric.

name: Mini-BEHAVIOR
desc: Gridworld reimplementation of BEHAVIOR semantics for fast, low-cost ablation of long-horizon decision making.

name: Habitat 3.0
caps: human-robot collaboration; humanoid avatars; fast sim
desc: Adds simulated humanoid avatars and a human-in-the-loop tool to Habitat, enabling social rearrangement and social navigation evaluation.

name: PARTNR
desc: Large-scale household collaboration benchmark with spatial, temporal and heterogeneous-capability constraints, and paired human-in-the-loop trials.

name: Embodied Agent Interface (EAI)
verifier: Per-module error taxonomy over LTL goals
caps: goal interpretation; subgoal decomposition; action sequencing; transition modeling
desc: Decomposes LLM embodied decision making into four interchangeable modules and reports a fine-grained error taxonomy instead of a single success rate.

name: LoTa-Bench
verifier: Automatic execution success in AI2-THOR / VirtualHome
desc: Removes human plan grading by executing LLM-generated plans directly in simulators, making planner comparison cheap and repeatable.

name: EmbodiedBench
caps: high-level household; low-level manipulation; spatial; long-horizon
desc: Spans high-level household planning to low-level manipulation in one harness, with capability-sliced subsets for commonsense, spatial and long-horizon skills.

name: EmbodiedEval
caps: navigation; object interaction; attribute QA; social interaction
desc: Interactive evaluation of MLLMs as embodied agents in a unified simulator, covering navigation, interaction, attribute QA, spatial QA and social tasks.

name: TEACh
desc: Household tasks specified through human-human dialogue, so an agent must resolve underspecification by asking rather than assuming.

name: VLABench
desc: Language-conditioned manipulation tasks that deliberately require mesh-level world knowledge, common sense and multi-step reasoning, not just skill execution.

name: CookBench
scale: Cooking scenarios in a high-fidelity sim
caps: long-horizon planning; tool use; state tracking
desc: Long-horizon cooking scenarios that stress fine-grained state tracking and interdependent subgoals in a single continuous episode.

name: LEGENT / EmbodiedEval-style open worlds
desc: Open platform pairing generated 3D worlds with an embodied LLM agent loop, useful for building new task suites rather than a fixed leaderboard.

name: Meta-World
desc: Fifty tabletop manipulation tasks with fixed multi-task and meta-learning splits, still the default sanity check for policy generalization.

name: RLBench
desc: Hundred-task manipulation suite with unlimited scripted demonstrations, the base environment for many 3D policy papers.

name: CALVIN
caps: long-horizon language conditioning; zero-shot env transfer
desc: Language-conditioned long-horizon manipulation scored by how many consecutive instructions an agent completes, with an explicit unseen-environment split.

name: LIBERO
caps: lifelong learning; knowledge transfer; spatial/object/goal shift
desc: Separates distribution shift into spatial, object, goal and long-horizon suites to measure transfer and forgetting, not just peak success.

name: ManiSkill2
desc: Object-diverse manipulation with fast GPU-parallel rollouts, including deformable and soft-body tasks that most suites omit.

name: ManiSkill3
caps: GPU parallel sim; visual RL; throughput
desc: GPU-parallelized successor reaching very high visual-observation throughput, which changes what an RL or evaluation budget can cover.

name: VIMA-Bench
desc: Multimodal-prompt manipulation with four explicitly nested generalization levels, from placement shift to novel task composition.

name: COLOSSEUM
desc: Systematically perturbs color, texture, size, lighting, distractors and camera pose to measure which factor actually breaks a manipulation policy.

name: RoboCasa
caps: everyday kitchen tasks; generative assets; scaling study
desc: Large-scale kitchen simulation with generatively produced assets and scenes, designed to study how imitation performance scales with synthetic data.

name: ARNOLD
caps: continuous states; language grounding; novel-state generalization
desc: Grounds instructions in continuous target states (for example pour to a level) rather than discrete goals, with explicit unseen-state splits.

name: GemBench / 3D-LOTUS++
caps: novel placements; novel objects; novel tasks
desc: Four-level generalization ladder for language-conditioned manipulation ending in wholly unseen long-horizon tasks.

name: SIMPLER
verifier: Sim success rate calibrated to real success
desc: Sim environments built so that measured success correlates with real-robot success for the same checkpoint, making sim a proxy evaluator for VLAs.

name: RoboTwin
scale: Dual-arm tasks with generated expert data
desc: Paired real and simulated dual-arm setups with automatically generated expert trajectories, so sim scores can be checked against the physical twin.

name: RoboTwin 2.0
desc: Scales the twin approach with a large object library and strong randomization aimed specifically at cluttered, contact-rich bimanual settings.

name: BiGym
desc: Mobile bimanual household tasks driven by human-collected demonstrations rather than scripted policies, which makes the demo distribution realistically noisy.

name: GenManip
caps: policy vs. modular comparison; scene generation
desc: Compares end-to-end VLA policies against modular LLM-planner pipelines on the same generated tabletop scenarios.

name: VLMbench
desc: Automatically generated compositional manipulation instructions with a matched program-based evaluator.

name: Bi-DexHands
desc: Bimanual dexterous-hand tasks in Isaac Gym covering the high-DoF control regime that tabletop suites skip.

name: R2R (Room-to-Room VLN)
verifier: Success rate + SPL on unseen split
desc: The founding VLN benchmark: follow natural-language route instructions through panoramic real-scan graphs, with a held-out-building split.

name: RxR
caps: multilingual VLN; path fidelity; time-aligned pose
desc: Multilingual, densely time-aligned VLN with path-fidelity metrics that penalize reaching the goal by the wrong route.

name: VLN-CE
desc: Removes the navigation-graph assumption from VLN, exposing the large drop between waypoint-level and continuous-control navigation.

name: HM3D / Habitat ObjectNav
desc: Large real-scan dataset backing the Habitat ObjectNav challenge, the standard measure of semantic exploration in unseen buildings.

name: GOAT-Bench
verifier: Success + SPL over multimodal goal sequences
desc: Open-vocabulary lifelong navigation where goals arrive as category, language or image within one long episode, testing reuse of accumulated map memory.

name: HomeRobot OVMM
desc: Open-vocabulary mobile manipulation defined identically in simulation and on a real Hello Robot Stretch, making the sim-real gap the reported quantity.

name: GRUtopia
desc: City-scale simulated society with LLM-driven NPCs, extending embodied evaluation beyond the single-household setting.

name: AerialVLN
desc: Vision-language navigation for UAVs in city-scale outdoor scenes, where the action space is genuinely three-dimensional.

name: CityNav
desc: Language-goal aerial navigation grounded in real geographic map data rather than synthetic layouts.

name: HumanoidBench
caps: whole-body control; dexterous hands; hierarchical RL
desc: Simulated humanoid with two dexterous hands across locomotion and manipulation tasks, showing standard RL fails without learned low-level skills.

name: LocoMuJoCo
caps: imitation learning; locomotion; real motion data
desc: Imitation-learning benchmark for locomotion across quadrupeds, bipeds and musculoskeletal models with matched real motion-capture data.

name: Isaac Lab / Orbit
desc: Unified GPU-parallel robot-learning framework whose bundled locomotion and manipulation environments are the de facto sim baseline on NVIDIA stacks.

name: CARLA
verifier: Driving Score = route completion x infraction penalty
desc: The reference closed-loop driving simulator and public leaderboard, whose driving score multiplies route completion by an infraction penalty.

name: Bench2Drive
desc: Decomposes closed-loop driving into isolated skills (merging, overtaking, emergency brake, yielding) so a single aggregate score cannot hide a specific failure.

name: NAVSIM
desc: Data-driven non-reactive simulation whose PDM score correlates with closed-loop driving while costing far less than full simulation.

name: nuPlan
desc: Large-scale planning benchmark with both reactive and non-reactive closed-loop protocols over real logged driving.

name: Waymo Open Sim Agents Challenge
desc: Scores simulated traffic agents by distributional realism rather than single-trajectory error, the standard for evaluating learned sim agents.

name: DriveLM
desc: Structures driving reasoning as a graph of perception, prediction and planning questions so intermediate reasoning is scored, not only the final action.

name: LingoQA
desc: Free-form driving video QA with a learned judge validated against human ratings, covering action justification as well as perception.

name: nuScenes-QA
desc: Multi-modal QA over multi-view camera and LiDAR streams in outdoor driving scenes.

name: AutoEval
caps: autonomous real evaluation; reset policy; success detection
desc: Runs unattended real-robot policy evaluation using a learned reset policy and success classifier, with reported agreement against human-scored ground truth.

name: RoboArena
desc: Pools heterogeneous real-robot labs and aggregates pairwise preference judgments, because absolute success rates are not comparable across sites.

name: RoboChallenge
verifier: Remote scripted trials on shared hardware
desc: Provides remote access to a standardized real-robot cell so external teams can evaluate policies without owning hardware.

name: RobotArena ∞
desc: Converts user-recorded real videos into simulated evaluation environments, reporting greater discriminative power than narrow real-to-sim suites.

name: SafeAgentBench
caps: hazard rejection; implicit risk; long-horizon safety
desc: Pairs hazardous and safe instructions in an interactive simulator and scores both refusal and safe execution, finding refusal rates remain low.

name: BadRobot
verifier: Attack success rate on physical actions
desc: Shows that jailbreaking an embodied LLM produces physically consequential actions, and measures attack success on the resulting behaviour.

name: IS-Bench
desc: Scores safety over the whole execution process rather than the final state, catching agents that reach a safe goal through an unsafe intermediate step.

name: EARBench
desc: Automates generation and assessment of physical-risk scenarios for foundation-model-driven embodied systems.

name: Open X-Embodiment / RT-X
verifier: Not a benchmark: shared training corpus
desc: Pooled cross-embodiment robot dataset; treat as a training substrate, not an evaluation - reporting numbers on its held-out splits is not a benchmark result.

name: DROID
verifier: Not a benchmark: shared training corpus
desc: Large in-the-wild manipulation dataset on a standardized hardware platform, widely used as a pretraining set and as the basis for real evaluation cells.

name: AgiBot World Colosseo
desc: Large-scale real-robot dataset with an associated challenge, focused on dexterous bimanual tasks in structured real environments.

name: AI2-THOR
desc: Interactive household simulator underlying ALFRED, SafeAgentBench, LoTa-Bench and much of the LLM-agent literature.

name: Habitat-Lab / Habitat 2.0
desc: High-throughput embodied simulation stack whose rearrangement tasks and ObjectNav definitions are reused by most navigation benchmarks.

name: robosuite
desc: Modular MuJoCo manipulation framework that RoboCasa, robomimic and many task suites build on.

name: robomimic
desc: Standardized study of offline imitation from human demonstrations, useful for isolating data quality from algorithm choice.
